html:
The Squaxin are a Southern Coast Salish people of the southern inlets of Puget Sound in Washington, around today's Shelton and Olympia. Their ancestors were several groups, each tied to one of the sound's southern inlets, among them the Squaxin, Sahewamish and T'Peeksin; together they call themselves the People of the Water.

They fished for salmon, gathered shellfish and travelled the inlets by canoe. In 1854 their leaders signed the Treaty of Medicine Creek, which left them only small Squaxin Island as a reservation. Few could live there, and most families drifted back to the inlets and nearby towns. Their neighbours were the Nisqually and Puyallup, who signed the same treaty, and the Skokomish. The Squaxin Island Tribe today is based at Kamilche.
